outline:
Explore the systems behind everyday life and explain sustainability concepts in English. Students evaluate information, discuss issues, lead classmates in an activity, and reflect on their experience of the 2030 SDGs Game and what it reveals about larger systems.

Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, you will be able to:
1. Recognize how everyday life is shaped by larger systems.
2. Use English to explain a sustainability issue, evaluate information, and lead an activity that helps others discuss and learn about the issue.
3. Reflect in writing on your experience of the 2030 SDGs Game and what it reveals about larger systems.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction to systems
Week 2: Misinformation
Week 3: Fact-Checking
Week 4: Consumption and Waste
Week 5: Accessibility and Access; introduce facilitation and share interests
Week 6: Sustainability Playground Workshop; teams and teaching dates announced
Week 7: No class meeting; prepare facilitation with your team
Week 8: Student-led facilitation, Groups 1–2
Week 9: Student-led facilitation, Groups 3–4
Week 10: Student-led facilitation, Groups 5–6
Week 11: Student-led facilitation, Groups 7–8
Week 12: Student-led facilitation, Groups 9–10
Week 13: Student-led facilitation, Groups 11–12
Week 14: Student-led facilitation, Group 13; 2030 SDGs Game
Week 15: 2030 SDGs Game
Week 16: Reflection and game reflection sharing; final reflection due Sunday 18:00 Taiwan time
Schedule adjustments will be announced in advance.
scorePolicy:
Participation & Preparedness: 30%
Class Work Portfolio: 20%
Student-Led Facilitation: 20%
SDGs Game Reflection: 30%

Participation includes structured discussion, in-class tasks, respectful listening and preparedness. The portfolio is checked at mid-semester and semester end for completion and engagement; facilitation and final reflection work are not graded again in the portfolio.

Facilitation: In 12 pairs and one trio, lead a 30–40-minute session using a text, activity and discussion. Shared work accounts for 60% of the facilitation score and individual explanation and contribution 40%. Everyone prepares, explains and facilitates.

SDGs Game Reflection: Write an individual 350–500-word reflection on your experience of the 2030 SDGs Game. Use specific moments from the game to explore your decisions and what they reveal about larger systems. Share briefly in Week 16. Submit the completed reflection by Sunday of Week 16 at 18:00 Taiwan time. Assessment values observation, reflection, systems thinking and clear communication.

Follow AI guidance for each task. Facilitation permits AI for research, brainstorming, translation and presentation design; students must understand and explain what they teach.
materials: Instructor-provided readings, course slides and the shared class notebook; materials selected for the issues explored.
